_comment: Operational gas balances, and who has to do something about them.
This file predates the smart-wallet migration and still describes the
world before it, which is deliberate: both worlds exist at once while the
cutover is pending, and the backend narrows this automatically rather than
needing the file edited at the moment of the switch.
BEFORE the cutover, every account below signs its own transactions and so
needs CELO. Falling under min_celo triggers a top-up back to
top_up_to_celo, paid out of the faucet, in 'priority' order when the
faucet cannot cover everything at once.
AFTER it, our accounts are smart wallets and their transactions are paid
for by the paymaster. They need no gas at all, so their floors stop
applying — a protocol account at zero CELO is then working as designed,
and alerting on it would bury the one alert that matters. The accounts
that keep a floor are the ones marked 'needs_gas', and there is exactly
one: the paymaster, which is the account doing the sponsoring.
Top-ups also stop entirely at that point, and cannot be otherwise. The
balance that used to fund everything is in a smart wallet, and moving CELO
out of one is itself a sponsored transaction that the paymaster pays for —
so the only account still needing gas is the one whose top-up would depend
on it already having some. That circle does not close. The paymaster is
funded by a person, and this service's job narrows to saying when.
What still needs watching after the cutover:
- the paymaster's CELO, which only a person can refill;
- the faucet's SFLUV, read from the smart wallet the money moved into.
Top-ups are capped at one transaction per account per minute regardless of
balances, and an account topped up twice inside two minutes raises a drain
alert rather than being funded quietly.
'enabled' is the switch for moving funds and starts off, which is the way
to watch this before trusting it with transfers. Per-account 'auto_top_up'
false does the same for one account. FUNDING_AUTO_TOPUP in the environment
overrides this field either way, so the switch can be flipped on a running
deployment without editing this file; setting it false is the kill switch.
'alerts' is separate and defaults to ON even when it is absent: moving
money should take an opt-in, being told it is about to run out should not.

accounts.name: Paymaster sponsor
accounts.notes: The only account that needs CELO once our own wallets are sponsored, and the only one a person has to top up. First in line, always. Pays gas for every sponsored user transaction, so customer payments to merchants all stop together when it is empty - this is the account whose exhaustion stopped payments with no warning. It is the paymaster contract's sponsor() and belongs to Citizen Wallet, not us: we cannot sign for it, but it is an EOA and anyone may fund it. At roughly 0.03 CELO a transaction, the 1 CELO floor is about thirty transactions of warning and the 6 CELO target about two hundred.

accounts.name: Redeemer admin
accounts.notes: Grants REDEEMER_ROLE to approved merchant locations. Empty means a newly approved merchant silently cannot take payment - until the cutover, after which its grants go through its smart wallet, it needs no gas, and this floor stops applying.

accounts.name: Admin
accounts.notes: Watched, not funded: it signs rarely and is worth a person noticing. Needs no gas after the cutover either, so this floor also stops applying then.
